### GitHub Issue #7966 Failure when trying to call __repr__ because __iter__ is called?
## 1. Problem

The following code 

```python
class A:
    def __iter__(self):
        raise ValueError()

    def __eq__(self, o: object) -> bool:
        return self is o


def test_a():
    assert A() == A()
```

...will throw:

```
    def test_a():
>       assert A() == A()
E       assert <tests.test_p...0019C132F1490> == <tests.test_p...0019C132F12B0>
E         (pytest_assertion plugin: representation of details failed: XXX\test_pp.py:3: ValueError.
E          Probably an object has a faulty __repr__.)
```

...because `__iter__` is called in order to `repr()` the object?

Is there a way to avoid `__iter__` being called when a test fails?

## 2. Setup

#### Python 3.8.2 | pytest 6.1.1

### GitHub Issue #11091 Documentation: confusion between `--junit-xml` and `--junitxml`
The docs and cli help are a bit confusing around the `--junitxml`/`--junit-xml` cli option (and probably some comparable options).


`pytest --help` only mentions `--junit-xml=path` (e.g. also see https://docs.pytest.org/en/7.1.x/reference/reference.html#command-line-flags):
```text
  --junit-xml=path      Create junit-xml style report file at given path
```

However, most examples in the docs (and mosts tests) use `--junitxml`, e.g. https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/0ded3297a9749aabad7d3c2447dce98321741dda/doc/en/how-to/output.rst#creating-junitxml-format-files :

```rst
To create result files which can be read by Jenkins_ or other Continuous
integration servers, use this invocation:

.. code-block:: bash

    pytest --junitxml=path

to create an XML file at ``path``.
```

This was quite confusing to me as it seemed there was a typo somewhere and I lost time just to figure out that they are aliases actually:

https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/0ded3297a9749aabad7d3c2447dce98321741dda/src/_pytest/junitxml.py#L384-L386



Wouldn't it be better to stick to one of the two everywhere or at least more explicitly mention that they are aliases?
